title: Throttle window desync between API gateway and runtime causing elevated 429s
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers (Dedicated and some Private deployments) experienced a spike in 429 Throttled responses over a ~90 minute window. Root cause investigation shows inconsistent burst-window semantics between the API gateway's local token bucket and the downstream inference runtime's enforcement, causing gateways to throttle traffic more aggressively than the runtime intended. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, patch rollout, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy a client workload that sends short spikes of concurrent requests (50 qps bursts for 10s) to a model endpoint with burst allowances configured in the control plane.
2) Observe gateway-side 429 responses while runtime logs show accepted inflight requests and no runtime-side hard rejects.
3) Reproduce in Dedicated staging by toggling the gateway-local cache TTL to simulate out-of-sync config propagation.

impact: High - multiple paying Dedicated customers observed degraded SLA due to unexpected throttling. Some requests that should have proceeded were dropped at the gateway layer. Private customers with older agent versions were affected longer because their agent's policy TTL prevented quick application of the corrected config semantics.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: applied gateway fallback to use centralized token-bucket semantics (control-plane authoritative) for all newly established connections. 2) Short-term: pushed config change to reduce gateway aggressiveness and extended cache refresh frequency. 3) Medium-term: release hotfix to normalize burst_window units across gateway and runtime and add a compatibility shim.
root_cause: A unit/interpretation mismatch introduced during a recent change to burst window handling: the runtime interprets burst_window as milliseconds in the new schema, while the gateway continued to interpret it as seconds. The gateway's local cache TTL and versioning logic also allowed a stale policy to persist during rollout, so some proxy instances used the old semantics when the runtime had already switched to the new one. Additionally, Private deployment agents had a longer policy refresh interval and an unrelated bug in deserialization that caused dropped config updates, prolonging customer impact.
fix_summary: Add compatibility layer in gateway: detect control-plane policy schema version and convert burst_window units at read-time. Tighten local cache TTL and add versioned invalidation. Patch runtime to accept both units for a grace period and log schema mismatches to a dedicated metric. Include unit tests and an e2e test that simulates mixed-version gateways.
deployment_plan: 1) Merge PRs behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to hosted control-plane and enable in a single region (us-west-2) for 2h observation. 3) If metrics stable, roll GA to remaining hosted regions sequentially. 4) Schedule Dedicated pool update during low-traffic windows with canary subsets (5% -> 25% -> 100%), monitor token-drop and 429 metrics. 5) Coordinate Private customer agent update: publish agent patch and provide a migration guide and CLI flag to force immediate policy refresh. 6) Remove compatibility shim after 6 weeks when adoption threshold reached.
rollback_plan: If the hotfix causes unexpected regressions: 1) disable feature flag and revert gateway shim via control-plane toggle to restore previous behavior. 2) For Dedicated, roll back pool instances to previous stable image. 3) Communicate rollback to affected customers and CS. 4) Apply temporary control-plane policy override to set safe burst_window values until full rollback completes.
postmortem_actions: Tighten schema change process: require cross-team schema migration plan and compatibility tests.
Add automated e2e test simulating mixed-version policy interpretation during rollout.
Shorten default gateway policy TTL and add explicit cache invalidation endpoint.
Instrument a dedicated metric for policy-schema-mismatch occurrences and alert if >0 in production.
Update runbook for rate-limiting incidents with specific gateway vs runtime investigation checklist.
